title: How to help kids navigate friendship, with Eileen Kennedy-Moore, PhD

sentences.en: Having good friends is key to kids' mental health and well-being, just as it is for adults.
sentences.zh: 拥有好朋友对孩子的心理健康和幸福感至关重要，就像对成年人一样。

sentences.en: But it isn't always easy to navigate the complicated social dynamics of elementary, middle, or high school.
sentences.zh: 但要驾驭小学、初中或高中复杂的社交动态并不总是那么容易。

sentences.en: Today we're going to talk with an expert on kids' friendships about how children make and keep friends, and how parents can help support them as they do.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将与一位儿童友谊专家探讨孩子们是如何结交并维持友谊的，以及父母如何为他们提供支持。

sentences.en: So, when do kids start to form real friendships?
sentences.zh: 那么，孩子从什么时候开始形成真正的友谊呢？

sentences.en: How does their understanding of friendship evolve as they grow from young children to teens?
sentences.zh: 随着他们从幼儿成长为青少年，他们对友谊的理解又是如何演变的？

sentences.en: Do all kids need a best friend?
sentences.zh: 所有的孩子都需要一个最好的朋友吗？

sentences.en: What do you do if your child is being bullied or excluded by a peer group?
sentences.zh: 如果你的孩子受到同龄人的欺凌或排挤，你该怎么办？

sentences.en: What if your kid is the one doing the excluding?
sentences.zh: 如果排挤别人的孩子恰好是你的孩子，那又该怎么办？

sentences.en: What happens when your child has a friend you don't like or who doesn't treat them well?
sentences.zh: 当你的孩子交了一个你不喜欢，或者对他们不够好的朋友时，会发生什么？

sentences.en: And how do kids navigate arguments with friends and even the inevitable friendship breakup?
sentences.zh: 孩子们又是如何处理与朋友之间的争吵，甚至是不可避免的友谊破裂的呢？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Eileen Kennedy-Moore, a clinical psychologist and author based in Princeton, New Jersey.
sentences.zh: 今天我的嘉宾是艾琳·肯尼迪-摩尔博士，她是一位常驻新泽西州普林斯顿的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: She's written many books for children and parents about friendship, including
sentences.zh: 她为儿童和家长撰写了许多关于友谊的书籍，包括

sentences.en: Growing Friendships, A Kid's Guide to Making and Keeping Friends, and Kid Confidence, Help Your Child Make Friends, Build Confidence, and Develop Real Self-Esteem.
sentences.zh: 《培养友谊：儿童结交与维持友谊指南》以及《儿童自信心：帮助你的孩子结交朋友、建立自信并培养真正的自尊》。

sentences.en: She's also the creator of the podcast Kids Ask Dr. Friendtastic, where she answers questions directly from children about making and keeping friends,
sentences.zh: 她还是播客《孩子问友谊博士》的创作者，在节目中她直接回答孩子们关于结交和维持友谊的问题，

sentences.en: offering gentle, practical, and research-based advice on all kinds of friendship issues.
sentences.zh: 并就各种友谊问题提供温和、实用且基于研究的建议。

sentences.en: Dr. Kennedy-Moore has been featured in major print, radio, and TV outlets, including The New York Times, The Washington Post, and CNN.com.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪-摩尔博士曾登上多家主流平面、广播和电视媒体，包括《纽约时报》、《华盛顿邮报》和 CNN.com。

sentences.en: Dr. Kennedy-Moore, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪-摩尔博士，感谢您今天参加我们的节目。

sentences.en: My pleasure, Kim.
sentences.zh: 我的荣幸，金。

sentences.en: I'm delighted to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: At what age do kids start forming real friendships, not just playing with the toddler who happens to be next to them in the sandbox?
sentences.zh: 孩子从几岁开始形成真正的友谊，而不是仅仅和沙坑里碰巧在旁边的幼儿一起玩耍？

sentences.en: And how does their understanding of friendship change as they get older?
sentences.zh: 随着年龄增长，他们对友谊的理解又是如何改变的？

sentences.en: Well, you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: There is a developmental sequence in children's friendships.
sentences.zh: 儿童友谊的发展确实有一个序列。

sentences.en: And at the toddler ages, we have that love the one you're with stage, where they're just playing whoever's around.
sentences.zh: 在幼儿时期，我们处于“爱身边的人”阶段，他们只是和周围的人一起玩。

sentences.en: And then they expand to what I call the I want it my way stage.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会进入我所说的“我行我素”阶段。

sentences.en: And this is for ages about three to six, where they have very limited ability to see someone else's perspective.
sentences.zh: 这大约是三到六岁的阶段，他们从他人角度看问题的能力非常有限。

sentences.en: And they assume that kids, other children, see things exactly the way they do.
sentences.zh: 他们认为其他孩子看待事物的方式与他们完全一样。

sentences.en: So when another kid wants something else, it kind of blows their mind.
sentences.zh: 所以当另一个孩子想要别的东西时，他们会感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: Then we move into from seven to 12, the two-way fair weather cooperation, which I call the by the rules kind of friendship.
sentences.zh: 接着我们进入七到十二岁的“双向公平合作”阶段，我称之为“按规则办事”的友谊。

sentences.en: And here, kids have more of an idea of reciprocity, but they're very strict in how they do it.
sentences.zh: 在这个阶段，孩子们对互惠有了更多的概念，但他们执行起来非常死板。

sentences.en: It's very much quid pro quo.
sentences.zh: 这非常讲究等价交换。

sentences.en: If I do something nice for you, you'd better do something nice for me, or everything falls apart.
sentences.zh: 如果我为你做点好事，你最好也为我做点好事，否则一切都会分崩离析。

sentences.en: They tend to be very judgmental of both themselves and others.
sentences.zh: 他们往往对自己和他人都有很强的评判性。

sentences.en: This is also the age where we see a lot of those secret clubs, where, right, they're talking forever about who's in and who's out and what the
sentences.zh: 这也是我们看到很多秘密俱乐部的年龄段，他们会没完没了地讨论谁能加入、谁被排除在外，以及

sentences.en: rules are in the club never actually does anything.
sentences.zh: 俱乐部里的规则，但实际上什么也没做。

sentences.en: A friend of mine said that her son at this stage was in a band.
sentences.zh: 我的一位朋友说，她儿子在这个阶段参加了一个乐队。

sentences.en: And they would talk about, you know, whose role everybody was playing.
sentences.zh: 他们会讨论每个人扮演什么角色。

sentences.en: And but none of played an instrument.
sentences.zh: 但其实他们谁也不会演奏乐器。

sentences.en: Perfect.
sentences.zh: 太完美了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then when we get from about age 12 up, we have those more mature friendships where it's through thick or thin.
sentences.zh: 然后到了十二岁左右，我们有了更成熟的友谊，也就是那种风雨同舟的友谊。

sentences.en: But and they put a high value on closeness with friends, they can accept and even appreciate differences between themselves and other friends.
sentences.zh: 他们非常重视与朋友的亲密关系，能够接受甚至欣赏自己与朋友之间的差异。

sentences.en: And they're not quite as possessive as the earlier stages.
sentences.zh: 而且他们不像早期阶段那样占有欲那么强。

sentences.en: So this is more like what we adults would think of as a friendship.
sentences.zh: 所以这更接近我们成年人所认为的友谊。

sentences.en: At an earlier age, if a friend has another friend, they feel deeply betrayed.
sentences.zh: 在更小的时候，如果一个朋友有了另一个朋友，他们会感到深深的背叛。

sentences.en: But once they move into the teen years, they understand that, yeah, we can have multiple friends.
sentences.zh: 但一旦进入青少年时期，他们就会明白，是的，我们可以拥有多个朋友。

sentences.en: How did you decide to focus on children's friendship as a subject for your books and your podcast?
sentences.zh: 您是如何决定将儿童友谊作为您书籍和播客的主题的呢？

sentences.en: What got you interested in this area?
sentences.zh: 是什么让您对这个领域感兴趣？

sentences.en: Well, you could say it came from a personal place, because when my family was growing up, we moved about every three years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你可以说这源于个人经历，因为我小时候，我们家大约每三年搬一次家。

sentences.en: So I became an expert at making friends at a very young age, kind of because I had to.
sentences.zh: 所以我在很小的时候就成了结交朋友的专家，某种程度上是因为我不得不这样做。

sentences.en: And then as an adult, I studied the research about children's friendships.
sentences.zh: 后来作为成年人，我研究了关于儿童友谊的课题。

sentences.en: And I'm a clinical psychologiSt. So in my practice, I hear every day, every week about the concerns that children have about their friendships.
sentences.zh: 我是一名临床心理学家，所以在我的诊所里，我每天、每周都能听到孩子们对友谊的担忧。

sentences.en: Getting along with other people is hard.
sentences.zh: 与人相处很难。

sentences.en: We adults haven't managed world peace or even perfect marriages.
sentences.zh: 我们成年人还没能实现世界和平，甚至连完美的婚姻都难以维持。

sentences.en: So it's understandable that kids would also struggle in their relationships.
sentences.zh: 所以孩子在人际关系中挣扎也是可以理解的。

sentences.en: But what the research tells us is that friendship is kind of the answer to everything.
sentences.zh: 但研究告诉我们，友谊几乎是解决一切问题的答案。

sentences.en: If you want a child to feel happier, help them make friends.
sentences.zh: 如果你想让孩子感到更快乐，就帮他们结交朋友。

sentences.en: If you want them to cope better with stress, friends.
sentences.zh: 如果你想让他们更好地应对压力，就让他们交朋友。

sentences.en: If you want them to be more engaged with school, less likely to be bullied, friends.
sentences.zh: 如果你想让他们更投入学习，减少被欺凌的可能性，那就让他们交朋友。

sentences.en: So we really do want to do what we can to support children's friendships.
sentences.zh: 所以我们确实想尽我们所能去支持孩子的友谊。

sentences.en: So speaking of that support, what can parents do that will help their children make friends that will back them up and give them the knowledge and the wherewithal to
sentences.zh: 说到这种支持，父母能做些什么来帮助孩子结交朋友，让他们有后盾，并给予他们知识和能力去

sentences.en: go out in the world and, you know, buddy up?
sentences.zh: 走向世界，去结交伙伴呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, Kim, a lot of times in my practice, I see parents who feel very helpless when their kid is having a friendship rough spot.
sentences.zh: 你知道，金，在我的诊所里，我经常看到父母在孩子遇到友谊困境时感到非常无助。

sentences.en: And it's like, well, I can't make friends for them.
sentences.zh: 他们会觉得，我没法替他们交朋友。

sentences.en: And that's true.
sentences.zh: 这确实是真的。

sentences.en: But there are a lot of things that we as parents or as people who care about kids can do to support and nurture their friendships.
sentences.zh: 但作为父母，或者作为关心孩子的人，我们有很多事情可以做，来支持和培养他们的友谊。

sentences.en: What fuels that development of children's friendships from the love the one you're with friendships of the toddler years to the more intimate and lasting years of the teen years
sentences.zh: 是什么推动了儿童友谊从幼儿时期的“爱身边的人”发展到青少年时期更亲密、更持久的友谊呢？

sentences.en: is an increasing ability to understand someone else's perspective.
sentences.zh: 是理解他人视角的能力在不断增强。

sentences.en: So that's something that we adults can help with a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们成年人可以提供很大帮助的地方。

sentences.en: When we talk through a situation with them, we always want to start with empathy because our children need that understanding and that sense of being held and supported.
sentences.zh: 当我们和他们讨论情况时，我们总是想从同理心开始，因为我们的孩子需要那种被理解、被支持的感觉。

sentences.en: But then we can help them to imagine the other child's perspective.
sentences.zh: 但随后我们可以帮助他们想象对方孩子的视角。

sentences.en: How do you think he felt why that when that happened?
sentences.zh: 你觉得当那件事发生时，他是什么感受？

sentences.en: Why do you think she did that?
sentences.zh: 你觉得她为什么那样做？

sentences.en: And this is kind of expanding their awareness, developing their theory of mind.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上是在扩展他们的意识，发展他们的心智理论。

sentences.en: We can also talk about feelings as they come up in daily life, or as we see it in a movie or a story.
sentences.zh: 我们也可以在日常生活中，或者在电影或故事中看到相关情节时，谈论感受。

sentences.en: And don't do it so much that you ruin the story.
sentences.zh: 不要做得太过火，以免破坏了故事的乐趣。

sentences.en: But we can talk about why do you think they did that?
sentences.zh: 但我们可以讨论，你觉得他们为什么那样做？

sentences.en: Or how do you think you reacted there?
sentences.zh: 或者你觉得你在那里是怎么反应的？

sentences.en: Or gosh, she seemed really excited about that.
sentences.zh: 或者天哪，她看起来对那件事真的很兴奋。

sentences.en: Whatever we see and help them to be aware of this whole inner world.
sentences.zh: 无论我们看到什么，都要帮助他们意识到这个丰富的内心世界。

sentences.en: There's research that when parents talk more about feelings, kids become better able to understand another person's perspective.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，当父母更多地谈论感受时，孩子就越能理解他人的视角。

sentences.en: Another thing we can do is place a high value on friendship.
sentences.zh: 我们能做的另一件事是高度重视友谊。

sentences.en: Let them see us making time.
sentences.zh: 让他们看到我们抽出时间来经营友谊。

sentences.en: I know you're busy, so am I, we're all busy.
sentences.zh: 我知道你很忙，我也是，我们都很忙。

sentences.en: But make time for those friendships.
sentences.zh: 但要为这些友谊留出时间。

sentences.en: Let your child see you going out of your way to get together with friends, to do kind things for your neighbors, to put a priority on relationships.
sentences.zh: 让你的孩子看到你为了与朋友聚会、为邻居做善事、将人际关系放在首位而付出的努力。

sentences.en: And probably the single best thing we as parents can do for our kids to support their friendships is to help them have those one-on-one playdates.
sentences.zh: 而且我们作为父母能为孩子支持友谊所做的最好的一件事，可能就是帮助他们进行一对一的玩耍约会。

sentences.en: That's what really deepens the friendships, those one-on-one get-togethers.
sentences.zh: 那才是真正加深友谊的方式，那些一对一的聚会。

sentences.en: Now, in my practice, a lot of times kids will push back and say, oh, I don't really know the kid that well.
sentences.zh: 在我的诊所里，很多时候孩子会推脱说，哦，我和那个孩子不太熟。

sentences.en: That's okay.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: If you've had fun with them once, that's enough.
sentences.zh: 如果你和他们玩过一次，那就足够了。

sentences.en: You can invite them over.
sentences.zh: 你可以邀请他们过来。

sentences.en: So speaking of inviting them over and playdates, how has social media changed that behavior?
sentences.zh: 说到邀请他们过来和玩耍约会，社交媒体是如何改变这种行为的？

sentences.en: Are kids still having playdates or would they rather text and talk on their phones?
sentences.zh: 孩子们还在进行玩耍约会吗，还是他们更愿意发短信和打电话？

sentences.en: Well, I don't even mean talk on their phones.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我甚至不是指打电话。

sentences.en: I don't use their phones to talk.
sentences.zh: 他们不用手机通话。

sentences.en: They're not talking on their phones.
sentences.zh: 他们不在手机上聊天。

sentences.en: They kind of have an aversion to do that.
sentences.zh: 他们对那样做有一种抵触情绪。

sentences.en: It's really texting or messaging through one of the apps.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上是通过应用程序发短信或留言。

sentences.en: What research tells us is that social media in general supports and supplements children's real-life friendships.
sentences.zh: 研究告诉我们，社交媒体总体上支持并补充了孩子现实生活中的友谊。

sentences.en: And for most kids, that's what they do.
sentences.zh: 对大多数孩子来说，他们就是这样做的。

sentences.en: Of course, there are cases where they're just spending all their time on that or it brings them down.
sentences.zh: 当然，也有一些案例是他们把所有时间都花在上面，或者这让他们感到沮丧。

sentences.en: But it can't substitute for that in-person getting together.
sentences.zh: 但它无法替代那种面对面的聚会。

sentences.en: Inviting somebody over sends a powerful message that, hey, I like you enough to spend time with you outside of when we have to be together.
sentences.zh: 邀请某人过来传递了一个强有力的信号：嘿，我喜欢你，愿意在必须在一起的时间之外和你共度时光。

sentences.en: So it really is a lovely thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是一件美好的事情。

sentences.en: And even if the person says, no, you've still done that signaling that you are open to friendship.
sentences.zh: 即使对方拒绝了，你也已经发出了信号，表明你对友谊持开放态度。

sentences.en: Often, I find that an activity-based get-together is good because an activity-based get-together allows the activity
sentences.zh: 我经常发现，基于活动的聚会很好，因为基于活动的聚会可以让活动

sentences.en: to pass over any of the awkwardness because kids know what to do.
sentences.zh: 掩盖任何尴尬，因为孩子们知道该做什么。

sentences.en: Often at the beginning of a playdate, there's that awkward moment where one kid says to the other kid, what do you want to do?
sentences.zh: 通常在玩耍约会开始时，会有那种尴尬的时刻，一个孩子对另一个孩子说，你想做什么？

sentences.en: And the other kid says, I don't know, what do you want to do?
sentences.zh: 另一个孩子说，我不知道，你想做什么？

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: So we can get past that if you prep your kid beforehand.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你提前引导你的孩子，我们就可以克服这一点。

sentences.en: So have them think of two things that they might want to do with a friend.
sentences.zh: 让他们想出两件他们可能想和朋友一起做的事情。

sentences.en: And then when the friend arrives, you greet the friend and say, would you like to do A or B?
sentences.zh: 然后当朋友到达时，你迎接朋友并说，你想做A还是B？

sentences.en: And that allows the friend to get to playing together as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 这让朋友们能够尽快开始一起玩耍。

sentences.en: And that's what research shows whether they're likely to become closer friends is how much time do they spend playing together.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，他们是否可能成为更亲密的朋友，取决于他们在一起玩耍的时间有多少。

sentences.en: We also want to emphasize to our child that you are the hoSt. So it's your job to make sure your guest has a good time.
sentences.zh: 我们还要向孩子强调，你是主人，所以确保客人玩得开心是你的工作。

sentences.en: And how can you do that?
sentences.zh: 那你该怎么做呢？

sentences.en: So notice if the guest gets a little bored or gets frustrated, and that's a good time to suggest two more activities.
sentences.zh: 注意客人是否感到有点无聊或沮丧，那是建议另外两项活动的最佳时机。

sentences.en: Now, how does a parent's role change as the child gets older?
sentences.zh: 那么，随着孩子年龄增长，父母的角色是如何改变的？

sentences.en: What happens when you're dealing with, you know, a tween, an early teenage kid who is saying, Mom, I don't want to talk about this with you?
sentences.zh: 当你面对一个青春期前后的孩子，他说：“妈妈，我不想和你谈这个”时，会发生什么？

sentences.en: How can you still help these children?
sentences.zh: 你还能如何帮助这些孩子？

sentences.en: Usually when children resist talking about friendship issues is because they're afraid they're going to get lectured and scolded.
sentences.zh: 通常当孩子抵触谈论友谊问题时，是因为他们害怕被说教和责骂。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: So be very, very careful about that.
sentences.zh: 所以在这方面要非常非常小心。

sentences.en: Never criticize your child in front of other kids.
sentences.zh: 永远不要在其他孩子面前批评你的孩子。

sentences.en: There's actually studies that shows that that really hurts your child's social standing with their peers.
sentences.zh: 实际上有研究表明，这样做会严重损害你孩子在同龄人中的社会地位。

sentences.en: And we want to ask questions more than telling answers.
sentences.zh: 我们应该多提问，而不是直接给出答案。

sentences.en: When we're teaching our kids math, we don't say four.
sentences.zh: 当我们教孩子数学时，我们不会直接说四。

sentences.en: The answer is four, right?
sentences.zh: 答案是四，对吧？

sentences.en: We take, well, where's the numerator?
sentences.zh: 我们会问，分子在哪里？

sentences.en: Where's the denominator?
sentences.zh: 分母在哪里？

sentences.en: And we guide them through that.
sentences.zh: 然后我们引导他们完成计算。

sentences.en: This is the same thing with learning about getting along with peers.
sentences.zh: 学习如何与同龄人相处也是一样。

sentences.en: Start with empathy because they need you on your side.
sentences.zh: 从同理心开始，因为他们需要你站在他们这一边。

sentences.en: And pick your moment.
sentences.zh: 并且选择合适的时机。

sentences.en: Like when the child is really upset, that is not the time to say, see, didn't I tell you if you kept on like that, you're going to end up like this.
sentences.zh: 比如当孩子非常难过时，那不是说“你看，我没告诉你吗，如果你继续那样，你就会落得这个下场”的时候。

sentences.en: So not a good idea.
sentences.zh: 所以那不是个好主意。

sentences.en: We have to be first on their side.
sentences.zh: 我们必须首先站在他们这一边。

sentences.en: And then we can, we can ask questions.
sentences.zh: 然后我们可以提问。

sentences.en: The older the kid is, the more important it is to ask questions rather than give answers.
sentences.zh: 孩子年龄越大，提问就比给出答案更重要。

sentences.en: So you might say, so what do you think you might do?
sentences.zh: 所以你可以说，那你觉得你可能会怎么做？

sentences.en: Or how do you think she would react if you did that?
sentences.zh: 或者你觉得如果你那样做，她会有什么反应？

sentences.en: And help them to think it through rather than respond impulsively.
sentences.zh: 帮助他们思考清楚，而不是冲动行事。

sentences.en: Let's talk about best friends.
sentences.zh: 让我们谈谈最好的朋友。

sentences.en: You wrote a piece for psychology today, the column that you write for that outlet about whether kids need a best friend.
sentences.zh: 你为《今日心理学》写过一篇文章，也就是你为该媒体撰写的专栏，关于孩子是否需要一个最好的朋友。

sentences.en: What's your take?
sentences.zh: 你的看法是什么？

sentences.en: Is it important for kids to have a bestie?
sentences.zh: 孩子有最好的朋友很重要吗？

sentences.en: Or is it okay to have multiple friendships that just aren't that close?
sentences.zh: 或者拥有多段并不那么亲密的友谊也可以吗？

sentences.en: You know, every now and then in the popular literature, I see articles about, oh, kids shouldn't have best friends because I don't know.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我时不时会在大众文学中看到一些文章，说孩子不应该有最好的朋友，因为……我也不清楚原因。

sentences.en: I guess it's exclusive because then they might break up, which is true.
sentences.zh: 我想是因为这种关系具有排他性，他们可能会闹翻，这确实是真的。

sentences.en: But to me, having a best friend is a little bit like falling in love.
sentences.zh: 但在我看来，拥有一个最好的朋友有点像坠入爱河。

sentences.en: So we parents and adults, we don't get to control that for our children.
sentences.zh: 所以我们这些父母和成年人，无法为孩子掌控这种关系。

sentences.en: That's theirs.
sentences.zh: 那是属于他们自己的。

sentences.en: There are very few ways that children actually have autonomy, but this is one of them in the relationships that they choose.
sentences.zh: 孩子们真正拥有自主权的方式很少，但这正是其中之一，即他们选择建立的关系。

sentences.en: So about a third to a half of kids have best friends at any point.
sentences.zh: 所以，在任何时候，大约有三分之一到一半的孩子拥有最好的朋友。

sentences.en: There are payoffs to having a best friend in terms of how kids feel and their happiness and sense of belonging.
sentences.zh: 拥有最好的朋友在孩子的感受、幸福感和归属感方面是有回报的。

sentences.en: So it can be good.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能是件好事。

sentences.en: But of course, we know that there are different friendship qualities.
sentences.zh: 但当然，我们知道友谊的质量各不相同。

sentences.en: So a best friend who is getting our kid in trouble, maybe not so good, right?
sentences.zh: 如果一个最好的朋友让我们的孩子惹上麻烦，那可能就不太好了，对吧？

sentences.en: And there's also research showing that the peer group can have a negative influence on our kids.
sentences.zh: 而且也有研究表明，同伴群体可能对我们的孩子产生负面影响。

sentences.en: So we want to help our children to make good choices about whom they decide to be friends with.
sentences.zh: 所以我们希望帮助孩子在选择朋友时做出正确的决定。

sentences.en: So we can ask them questions like, how do you feel when you're with them?
sentences.zh: 我们可以问他们一些问题，比如：和他们在一起时你感觉如何？

sentences.en: Or do you feel like you can be yourself with them?
sentences.zh: 或者你觉得和他们在一起时能做真实的自己吗？

sentences.en: Or do you feel like you have to kind of fake it or hide things from them?
sentences.zh: 还是说你觉得必须伪装自己，或者对他们隐瞒一些事情？

sentences.en: Do you feel like these friends bring out the best in you and guide them towards thinking it through?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这些朋友能激发你最好的一面吗？引导他们去深入思考这些问题。

sentences.en: The one-on-one playdates can deepen the friendship spending time together.
sentences.zh: 一对一的玩耍约会可以通过共度时光来加深友谊。

sentences.en: Friendships take time.
sentences.zh: 友谊需要时间来培养。

sentences.en: I read one study and I never saw the original study.
sentences.zh: 我读过一项研究，但我从未见过原始研究。

sentences.en: So I don't know how true this is, but it was saying that for adult friendships, it takes 30
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道这有多真实，但它说对于成年人的友谊，需要30

sentences.en: hours to make a casual friend, 60 hours to make a close friend, and 90 hours to make an intimate friend.
sentences.zh: 个小时才能成为普通朋友，60个小时成为亲密朋友，90个小时成为知心朋友。

sentences.en: Isn't that amazing?
sentences.zh: 这不是很神奇吗？

sentences.en: So again, I can't vouch for how accurate those numbers are, but the point is it takes time to build that intimacy.
sentences.zh: 所以再说一次，我无法保证这些数字的准确性，但重点是建立这种亲密关系需要时间。

sentences.en: So a moment ago, you talked about maybe your kid has a best friend who's getting them in trouble, isn't a child you wish your kid were associating with.
sentences.zh: 刚才你提到，也许你的孩子有一个最好的朋友让他们惹上麻烦，不是你希望孩子交往的对象。

sentences.en: What can you as a parent do when you see your kid is with somebody who's just not a good influence or maybe isn't treating your kid very nicely?
sentences.zh: 当你发现孩子和某个影响不好，或者对孩子不太友善的人在一起时，作为父母该怎么办？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Sometimes kids stick to a not so good friend because they feel like they don't have any other options.
sentences.zh: 有时孩子们坚持和一个不太好的朋友在一起，是因为他们觉得没有其他选择。

sentences.en: So we can help our kid recognize how they feel when they're with that friend.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以帮助孩子认识到他们和那个朋友在一起时的感受。

sentences.en: You know, just raise the questions without saying, dump that kid.
sentences.zh: 你知道，只需提出问题，而不是直接说“甩掉那个孩子”。

sentences.en: As tempting as it is to say, you're not allowed to play with them.
sentences.zh: 尽管说“你不准和他们玩”很有诱惑力。

sentences.en: Be careful because you can have a Romeo and Julia effect, right?
sentences.zh: 但要小心，因为这可能会产生罗密欧与朱丽叶效应，对吧？

sentences.en: That they suddenly seem more attractive.
sentences.zh: 他们反而会显得更有吸引力。

sentences.en: And if your kid doesn't have any options, they may feel afloat.
sentences.zh: 如果你的孩子没有其他选择，他们可能会感到无所适从。

sentences.en: Also, they may go into school and say, my mom says I'm not allowed to play with you.
sentences.zh: 此外，他们可能会去学校说：“我妈妈说我不准和你玩。”

sentences.en: That's not so good.
sentences.zh: 那可不太好。

sentences.en: So I think the best option is to try to fan the flames on other possible friendships and let your
sentences.zh: 所以我认为最好的选择是尝试去点燃其他潜在友谊的火花，让你的

sentences.en: child experience the difference between an easier friendship, a kinder friendship, and this one that's more problematic.
sentences.zh: 孩子体验到轻松的友谊、友善的友谊与这种更有问题的友谊之间的区别。

sentences.en: You may want to help your child get involved in activities.
sentences.zh: 你可能想帮助孩子参与一些活动。

sentences.en: Kids make friends by doing fun things together.
sentences.zh: 孩子们通过一起做有趣的事情来交朋友。

sentences.en: So what is it that your child is interested in or might be interested in that they could do with other people?
sentences.zh: 那么你的孩子对什么感兴趣，或者可能对什么感兴趣，让他们可以和其他人一起做？

sentences.en: And that could be a way to find people, find their tribe, find ones that they could relate to and connect with.
sentences.zh: 这可能是一种找到同伴、找到志同道合的人、找到能产生共鸣和联系的人的方法。

sentences.en: What about when friendships end?
sentences.zh: 当友谊结束时该怎么办？

sentences.en: How do you help your child through a breakup with somebody who had been a friend?
sentences.zh: 你如何帮助孩子度过与曾经的朋友分手的难关？

sentences.en: And, you know, especially when you get to middle school and everybody goes off in different directions, how do you support your child through that?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，特别是当你到了初中，每个人都分道扬镳时，你该如何支持你的孩子？

sentences.en: Oh, it's hard, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 哦，这很难，不是吗？

sentences.en: And research tells us that among first graders, about half of friendships don't make it from September to June.
sentences.zh: 研究告诉我们，在一年级学生中，大约有一半的友谊无法从九月维持到六月。

sentences.en: And among fourth and eighth graders, one quarter of friendships don't laSt. So this is very, very common.
sentences.zh: 而在四年级和八年级学生中，四分之一的友谊无法持久。所以这非常非常普遍。

sentences.en: But children, by definition, lack perspective, right?
sentences.zh: 但孩子们从定义上来说缺乏视角，对吧？

sentences.en: They just haven't been around that long, and they haven't seen that much of the world.
sentences.zh: 他们活的时间还不够长，看过的世界也还不够多。

sentences.en: So the anguish that they're feeling right now feels like a forever thing, like they're always going to feel this sad.
sentences.zh: 所以他们此刻感受到的痛苦感觉像是永恒的，好像他们会永远这样难过下去。

sentences.en: Um, there, there are a couple of ideas here.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里有几个想法。

sentences.en: One is, we want to keep the door, if it was a good friendship before, we want to keep the door open to that reconnecting with that friend.
sentences.zh: 一是，如果之前是一段很好的友谊，我们希望留有余地，让那段友谊能够重修旧好。

sentences.en: So no slash and burn as, as, as things are going about, don't diss the other friend to everybody else at school.
sentences.zh: 所以不要在事情发生时就一刀切，不要在学校里对其他人诋毁那个朋友。

sentences.en: Um, and what we adults like the idea of kids always talking everything out.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们成年人喜欢孩子总是把一切都说清楚的想法。

sentences.en: But what research tells us is that that doesn't become negotiation and compromise doesn't become the main way that children resolve conflicts until age 19.
sentences.zh: 但研究告诉我们，直到19岁，谈判和妥协才成为孩子解决冲突的主要方式。

sentences.en: Before then, they either insist and give in, or they separate for a little bit, and then come back together and just be nice to each other.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，他们要么坚持己见，要么让步，或者分开一会儿，然后再聚在一起，互相友善对待。

sentences.en: And they kind of step over the conflict.
sentences.zh: 他们会跨过冲突。

sentences.en: And that's also very important, because one of the basic friendship skills is being able to forgive a friend for those unavoidable mistakes that they
sentences.zh: 这也是非常重要的，因为基本的友谊技能之一就是能够原谅朋友那些不可避免的错误，那些他们

sentences.en: make and that we're going to make also.
sentences.zh: 会犯的，我们也同样会犯的错误。

sentences.en: So when a child is going through a friendship breakup, and this is, this can be as bad as a romantic breakup for an adult, like the pain is real, we want to empathize with them.
sentences.zh: 所以当孩子经历友谊破裂时，这可能和成年人的浪漫关系破裂一样糟糕，痛苦是真实的，我们需要对他们表示同情。

sentences.en: Extra time with family can be a good consolation that yes, you're still wanted, you're still loved, you still belong.
sentences.zh: 与家人多相处可以是一种很好的慰藉，让他们知道：是的，你仍然被需要，你仍然被爱，你仍然属于这里。

sentences.en: That can be very, very helpful.
sentences.zh: 这会非常有帮助。

sentences.en: But we also might want to create opportunities for them to make other friends.
sentences.zh: 但我们也可能想为他们创造结交其他朋友的机会。

sentences.en: And just leave the door open, that maybe at a later point, they can reconnect.
sentences.zh: 并留有余地，也许在以后的某个时候，他们可以重新建立联系。

sentences.en: I worked with a kid once where he and another boy were best, best friends.
sentences.zh: 我曾经和一个孩子一起工作，他和另一个男孩是最好的朋友。

sentences.en: But then they did different sports.
sentences.zh: 但后来他们参加了不同的运动。

sentences.en: And they kind of drifted apart.
sentences.zh: 他们就渐渐疏远了。

sentences.en: And my boy was just really, really hurt by this.
sentences.zh: 我的那个孩子为此感到非常非常受伤。

sentences.en: And then time went on a couple of years, and they started doing the same sport again.
sentences.zh: 后来过了几年，他们又开始参加同一项运动了。

sentences.en: And they reconnected.
sentences.zh: 他们又重新建立了联系。

sentences.en: So if it was a good friendship once, chances are, it may rekindle.
sentences.zh: 所以如果曾经是一段很好的友谊，很有可能，它会重燃火花。

sentences.en: What if you discover, you see signs maybe that your child is the one who is being mean to other kids or excluding other children?
sentences.zh: 如果你发现，看到迹象表明你的孩子是对其他孩子刻薄或排挤其他孩子的那个人，该怎么办？

sentences.en: How do you deal with that?
sentences.zh: 你如何处理这个问题？

sentences.en: Oh, that feels awful, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 哦，那感觉太糟糕了，不是吗？

sentences.en: As a parent, and it's like, Oh, my gosh, what did I do?
sentences.zh: 作为父母，会觉得：天哪，我做了什么？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: What's you know, how did I fail that this kid would do something mean to somebody else?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我怎么会失败到让这个孩子对别人做出刻薄的事？

sentences.en: But let me tell you an interesting study.
sentences.zh: 但让我告诉你一项有趣的研究。

sentences.en: The researchers got teachers to identify the kids who were especially aggressive or especially non aggressive.
sentences.zh: 研究人员让老师找出那些特别具有攻击性或特别不具攻击性的孩子。

sentences.en: And these were elementary age kids.
sentences.zh: 这些是小学年龄的孩子。

sentences.en: And then they video recorded the kids on the playground.
sentences.zh: 然后他们录下了孩子们在操场上的视频。

sentences.en: Like, I don't know how they got permission to do this.
sentences.zh: 就像，我不知道他们是怎么获得许可做这件事的。

sentences.en: But but they did.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实做了。

sentences.en: What they found was that those especially aggressive kids did some kind of mean behavior every two minutes.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，那些特别具有攻击性的孩子每两分钟就会做出某种刻薄的行为。

sentences.en: But those especially non aggressive kids, they did some kind of mean behavior every three minutes.
sentences.zh: 但那些特别不具攻击性的孩子，每三分钟也会做出某种刻薄的行为。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: So this is common.
sentences.zh: 所以这很常见。

sentences.en: Children's empathy is not fully developed.
sentences.zh: 孩子的同理心还没有完全发育成熟。

sentences.en: They're, they're not that good at imagining other people's perspective, they will get better with time.
sentences.zh: 他们不太擅长想象别人的视角，随着时间的推移，他们会变得更好。

sentences.en: If we think of ourselves, we are more empathic at age 29, than we were at 19 than we were
sentences.zh: 如果我们回想自己，我们在29岁时比19岁时更有同理心，比

sentences.en: at nine, you know, just more experience in the world gives us a greater capacity to empathize with others and the little frontal lo grows into so that helps.
sentences.zh: 9岁时也更有同理心，你知道，更多的生活经验给了我们更大的能力去同情他人，而且前额叶也在生长，所以这有帮助。

sentences.en: So it is normal that kids will make mistakes about getting along with people.
sentences.zh: 所以孩子在与人相处时犯错是很正常的。

sentences.en: And they also so their empathy isn't fully developed.
sentences.zh: 而且他们的同理心还没有完全发育成熟。

sentences.en: And they experiment with social power.
sentences.zh: 他们也在尝试社会权力。

sentences.en: That's not nice.
sentences.zh: 那并不好。

sentences.en: But it's also kind of like the baby throwing the spoon off the off the high chair just to see what happens, right?
sentences.zh: 但这也有点像婴儿把勺子从高脚椅上扔下去，只是为了看看会发生什么，对吧？

sentences.en: They're experimenting.
sentences.zh: 他们在实验。

sentences.en: What the what we don't want to do is say you're bad, and you're a bully and so forth, the just labeling the kid is bad is not useful.
sentences.zh: 我们不想做的是说“你很坏”、“你是个恶霸”等等，仅仅给孩子贴上坏标签是没有用的。

sentences.en: One of the principles that I use in my practice is that we can't help a child move forward by convincing them of their badness, right?
sentences.zh: 我在实践中使用的一个原则是，我们不能通过说服孩子他们很坏来帮助他们进步，对吧？

sentences.en: And when we're angry, that's often what we tend to be drawn to do is like, you keep doing these mean things, if you end up like keep on like this, you're going to end up like that.
sentences.zh: 当我们生气时，往往倾向于这样做，比如：你一直做这些刻薄的事，如果你继续这样下去，你最终会变成那样。

sentences.en: None of that is helpful, because it applies to the next chapter in the story is more meanness.
sentences.zh: 这些都没有帮助，因为它会导致故事的下一章是更多的刻薄。

sentences.en: Children learn, we also don't want to, you know, like blast them with a punishment, because children learn not through suffering, but by doing it right.
sentences.zh: 孩子们学习，我们也不想用惩罚来轰炸他们，因为孩子学习不是通过受苦，而是通过做正确的事。

sentences.en: So that's what we need to figure out is how can we get this kid back on track with being a kind child.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要弄清楚的是，我们如何才能让这个孩子回到做一个友善孩子的正轨上。

sentences.en: So one technique that I developed, which is probably the best thing I ever invented, because it works.
sentences.zh: 所以我开发了一种技巧，这可能是我发明过的最好的东西，因为它有效。

sentences.en: And it works with children, it works with spouses, it works with co authors, co workers.
sentences.zh: 它对孩子有效，对配偶有效，对合著者、同事也有效。

sentences.en: And it's called a soft criticism.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“温和批评”。

sentences.en: Now, the normal response to criticism is to defend, well, it's not my fault, and you do it too.
sentences.zh: 现在，对批评的正常反应是防御，比如：这不是我的错，你也会这样做。

sentences.en: And and you know, they do it more.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道，他们会做得更多。

sentences.en: So the soft criticism is designed to get around that normal defensiveness.
sentences.zh: 所以温和批评旨在绕过那种正常的防御心理。

sentences.en: And we start step one by giving an excuse.
sentences.zh: 我们从第一步开始，给出一个借口。

sentences.en: The excuse might the excuse says to the child that we know they're a good person with good intentions, even when they mess up.
sentences.zh: 这个借口向孩子传达了我们知道他们是一个有好意的好人，即使他们搞砸了。

sentences.en: Also, in order to think of an excuse, we have to stop, imagine their perspective that raises our empathy, lowers our anger, great place to start.
sentences.zh: 此外，为了想出一个借口，我们必须停下来，想象他们的视角，这提高了我们的同理心，降低了我们的愤怒，这是一个很好的起点。

sentences.en: Plus, just at a practical level, if we give them an excuse, they don't have to come up with one.
sentences.zh: 另外，从实际层面来看，如果我们给他们一个借口，他们就不必自己找借口了。

sentences.en: And we can just kind of step over that.
sentences.zh: 我们可以直接跨过那一关。

sentences.en: So you might say something like, I know you didn't mean to, you probably didn't realize, I get that you were trying to whatever it was.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以说些类似的话：我知道你不是故意的，你可能没意识到，我明白你当时是想……无论那是什么。

sentences.en: Then step two is the part we want, which is describe the problem.
sentences.zh: 然后第二步是我们想要的部分，即描述问题。

sentences.en: And here what you want to say is when you bad behavior, bad outcome.
sentences.zh: 在这里你想说的是：当你做出坏行为时，会有坏结果。

sentences.en: So an example might be, I get that you were really frustrated that that girl was saying that you couldn't sit at the table.
sentences.zh: 所以一个例子可能是：我明白你当时很沮丧，因为那个女孩说你不能坐在桌子旁。

sentences.en: And that's, that's a that was a mean thing to do.
sentences.zh: 那是一件很刻薄的事。

sentences.en: And you were really upset.
sentences.zh: 你当时真的很生气。

sentences.en: At the same time, when you shove her out of her chair, you could really hurt her and you're the one who ended up in trouble.
sentences.zh: 但同时，当你把她从椅子上推开时，你可能会真的伤害到她，而你自己最终惹上了麻烦。

sentences.en: So and then the third step, which is the most important step is we talk about moving forward.
sentences.zh: 所以，然后是第三步，这是最重要的一步，我们谈论如何向前看。

sentences.en: So you might say, what can you do to help her feel better?
sentences.zh: 所以你可以说：你能做些什么来帮助她感觉好一点？

sentences.en: Or what could you do instead if that happens again?
sentences.zh: 或者如果再次发生这种情况，你可以做些什么来代替？

sentences.en: Or what do you think could help in this situation?
sentences.zh: 或者你认为在这种情况下什么会有帮助？

sentences.en: So we're helping the child to think through options.
sentences.zh: 所以我们是在帮助孩子思考各种选择。

sentences.en: Research tells us that kids who tend to be aggressive, there are two characteristics from different studies.
sentences.zh: 研究告诉我们，倾向于攻击性的孩子，有来自不同研究的两个特征。

sentences.en: One of them is that they tend to assume that other people are doing things out of deliberate meanness.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是他们倾向于认为别人做事情是出于故意的刻薄。

sentences.en: And what I do in my practice is I talk about the maybe game.
sentences.zh: 我在实践中所做的是谈论“也许游戏”。

sentences.en: So maybe they're doing it out of deliberate meanness because they want you to suffer, but probably not.
sentences.zh: 所以也许他们这样做是出于故意的刻薄，因为他们想让你受苦，但可能不是。

sentences.en: Deliberate meanness, you know, real intentional cruelty is pretty rare.
sentences.zh: 故意的刻薄，你知道，真正的蓄意残忍是相当罕见的。

sentences.en: So what are some other reasons why they might have been doing that?
sentences.zh: 那么他们那样做还有什么其他原因吗？

sentences.en: And if we can get the child to think of other possibilities, it makes the deliberate meanness explanation less likely.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能让孩子想到其他可能性，就会降低“故意的刻薄”这种解释的可能性。

sentences.en: So for example, Jeffrey took your pencil.
sentences.zh: 例如，杰弗里拿走了你的铅笔。

sentences.en: Now maybe he did it out of deliberate meanness because he wanted you to suffer, but probably not.
sentences.zh: 现在也许他是出于故意的刻薄才这么做的，因为他想让你受苦，但可能不是。

sentences.en: What are some other possibilities?
sentences.zh: 还有什么其他可能性？

sentences.en: Maybe he just borrowed it for a second.
sentences.zh: 也许他只是借用一下。

sentences.en: Maybe he took it without realizing.
sentences.zh: 也许他没意识到就拿走了。

sentences.en: Maybe he thought it was his pencil.
sentences.zh: 也许他以为那是他的铅笔。

sentences.en: Maybe it actually was his pencil.
sentences.zh: 也许那实际上就是他的铅笔。

sentences.en: They wouldn't come up with that one.
sentences.zh: 他们自己是想不出这一点的。

sentences.en: So and then the other thing that these aggressive kids struggle with is they don't know any other options.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些攻击性孩子挣扎的另一件事是他们不知道其他选择。

sentences.en: So when we as parents can slow things down and in a calm moment, not when they're very heated, when they're very heated, we just empathize, empathize,
sentences.zh: 所以当我们作为父母能够放慢节奏，在冷静的时刻，而不是在他们非常激动的时候——当他们非常激动时，我们只是同情、同情、

sentences.en: empathize, but in a calm moment, help them to think of other options.
sentences.zh: 同情——但在冷静的时刻，帮助他们思考其他选择。

sentences.en: Or my favorite question, what can you do to help that person feel better?
sentences.zh: 或者我最喜欢的问题：你能做些什么来帮助那个人感觉好一点？

sentences.en: And then we get them back on track of being a good kid.
sentences.zh: 然后我们让他们回到做一个好孩子的正轨上。

sentences.en: Now, what should you do if you have a very shy child and you feel like your kid just isn't
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你有一个非常害羞的孩子，并且你觉得你的孩子只是不……该怎么办？

sentences.en: making friends and you're worried and you think, you know, she's just really unhappy or maybe she's not, maybe she seems fine, but she doesn't have friends.
sentences.zh: 交朋友时，如果你感到担心，觉得她真的很不开心，或者也许她并没有不开心，看起来挺好的，但就是没有朋友。

sentences.en: What should you as a parent do?
sentences.zh: 作为家长，你应该怎么做呢？

sentences.en: Be careful about labeling the child as shy because that makes it sound like it's something inherent and unchangeable.
sentences.zh: 要小心给孩子贴上“害羞”的标签，因为这听起来好像是某种与生俱来且无法改变的东西。

sentences.en: So you might use language like it takes you a little while to get comfortable in a new situation, or you like to watch first before you, you dive in.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以换种说法，比如“你在新环境里需要一点时间才能适应”，或者“你喜欢先观察一下，然后再加入进去”。

sentences.en: The other thing we have to keep in mind is that there are many ways to be social and not everybody has to be a bounding into the room, life of the party extrovert, right?
sentences.zh: 我们还要记住，社交的方式有很多种，并不是每个人都必须成为那种蹦蹦跳跳、活跃气氛的社交达人，对吧？

sentences.en: There is certainly room in the world for a quieter way of interacting.
sentences.zh: 这个世界上当然有安静的互动方式的一席之地。

sentences.en: We want to work with rather than against our child's natural tendencies.
sentences.zh: 我们想要顺应孩子的天性，而不是去对抗它。

sentences.en: So this might be by choosing activities that fit this child's interests.
sentences.zh: 所以，这可以通过选择符合孩子兴趣的活动来实现。

sentences.en: And then it's very easy for them, or it's easier for the child because the conversation comes naturally from whatever the activity is.
sentences.zh: 这样对他们来说会非常容易，或者说更容易，因为对话会自然而然地从活动中产生。

sentences.en: And that could be a way in.
sentences.zh: 这可能就是一种切入点。

sentences.en: Sometimes we want to help them learn specific skills, like how to give a friendly greeting.
sentences.zh: 有时我们想帮助他们学习具体的技能，比如如何友好地打招呼。

sentences.en: I might talk about four steps in this.
sentences.zh: 我可能会讲四个步骤。

sentences.en: So you smile to show that you're happy to see the person.
sentences.zh: 首先，你微笑，表示见到对方很高兴。

sentences.en: You look them in the eye, or if that's uncomfortable, you look them in the forehead.
sentences.zh: 你看着对方的眼睛，如果觉得不自在，就看对方的额头。

sentences.en: If you look people in the forehead right between the eyebrows, from a little bit of a distance, it looks the same as looking them in the eye.
sentences.zh: 如果你在稍微远一点的距离看人的额头，也就是眉毛中间的位置，看起来和看眼睛是一样的。

sentences.en: So that can be a way for kids who are uncomfortable with eye contact to do that.
sentences.zh: 所以对于那些不习惯眼神交流的孩子来说，这是一种可行的方法。

sentences.en: Then you say, hi, and you say the person's name, because that makes the greeting personal.
sentences.zh: 然后你说“嗨”，并叫出对方的名字，因为这样会让问候显得更亲切。

sentences.en: It's like, I'm happy to see you.
sentences.zh: 就像是在说：“见到你很高兴。”

sentences.en: Now, some kids will resist this.
sentences.zh: 当然，有些孩子会抗拒这样做。

sentences.en: I don't want to do that.
sentences.zh: “我不想那样做。”

sentences.en: It's weird.
sentences.zh: “这太奇怪了。”

sentences.en: So with those kids, I start a step back and say, okay, tomorrow, when you go into school, I just want you to count how many greetings you see.
sentences.zh: 对于这些孩子，我会退后一步说：“好吧，明天你去学校的时候，我只想让你数数你看到了多少次问候。”

sentences.en: And what they come back with is a mullion, right?
sentences.zh: 他们回来后会说，有无数次，对吧？

sentences.en: And they come to see that that is the expected behavior.
sentences.zh: 他们会明白这就是大家所期待的行为。

sentences.en: That is the typical behavior.
sentences.zh: 这是典型的行为。

sentences.en: So they're actually standing out by not greeting people.
sentences.zh: 所以，不跟人打招呼反而让他们显得格格不入。

sentences.en: Kids who feel anxious around their peers tend to look down and look away.
sentences.zh: 在同龄人面前感到焦虑的孩子往往会低头或看向别处。

sentences.en: And they're focused on their own distress.
sentences.zh: 他们专注于自己的不安。

sentences.en: But the message that they're sending to other kids is, I don't like you, and I don't want anything to do with you.
sentences.zh: 但他们传达给其他孩子的信号却是：“我不喜欢你，我不想和你扯上任何关系。”

sentences.en: That's not how they feel.
sentences.zh: 这并不是他们的真实感受。

sentences.en: But that's where they're communicating.
sentences.zh: 但这却是他们所传达出的信息。

sentences.en: So with these children, we can help them role play greetings until they feel comfortable doing them.
sentences.zh: 所以对于这些孩子，我们可以帮他们进行问候的角色扮演，直到他们感到自在为止。

sentences.en: And then maybe even set a goal of greet however many people each day.
sentences.zh: 甚至可以设定一个目标，每天问候多少人。

sentences.en: And little by little, they will become more comfortable with it.
sentences.zh: 慢慢地，他们就会对此感到更加自在。

sentences.en: There was another study that I read that was talking about socially anxious children.
sentences.zh: 我读过另一项关于社交焦虑儿童的研究。

sentences.en: And they found that there were two main groups.
sentences.zh: 他们发现主要有两个群体。

sentences.en: One group of these anxious kids withdrew and stayed by themselves.
sentences.zh: 其中一组焦虑的孩子会退缩，独自待着。

sentences.en: The other group was equally anxious, but they were in the mix of things.
sentences.zh: 另一组孩子同样焦虑，但他们会融入其中。

sentences.en: And they just kind of smiled and nodded.
sentences.zh: 他们只是微笑着点头。

sentences.en: And long term, those kids did just fine.
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，这些孩子表现得很好。

sentences.en: So with some of my clients, I'll say, all you have to do is smile and nod.
sentences.zh: 所以对于我的一些客户，我会说，你只需要微笑和点头就行了。

sentences.en: Sometimes you can help them to just learn some tips about how to have a conversation.
sentences.zh: 有时你可以帮他们学习一些关于如何进行对话的小技巧。

sentences.en: You can enter a group with a compliment, a sincere compliment.
sentences.zh: 你可以用一句赞美，一句真诚的赞美来加入一个群体。

sentences.en: It's like a little gift.
sentences.zh: 这就像一份小礼物。

sentences.en: And it tells the person, I like you.
sentences.zh: 它告诉对方：“我喜欢你。”

sentences.en: Also, we tend to like people who appreciate our finer qualities, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，我们往往会喜欢那些欣赏我们优点的人，对吧？

sentences.en: So it makes them like you a little bit better also.
sentences.zh: 所以这也会让他们更喜欢你一点。

sentences.en: Or there's another thing from research about how to join a group.
sentences.zh: 或者研究中还有关于如何加入群体的另一件事。

sentences.en: We adults tend to tell the kids, go over there and introduce yourself and ask if you can play.
sentences.zh: 我们成年人往往会告诉孩子：“过去做个自我介绍，问问能不能一起玩。”

sentences.en: No, this is not what happens on the playground.
sentences.zh: 不，操场上可不是这么回事。

sentences.en: So what they need to do is a sequence that I call watch, then blend.
sentences.zh: 所以他们需要做的是我称之为“观察，然后融入”的流程。

sentences.en: So watch what the other kids are doing, and then slide into the action conversation without interrupting it, without drawing attention to yourself.
sentences.zh: 观察其他孩子在做什么，然后滑入他们的活动或对话中，不要打断他们，也不要引起对他人的注意。

sentences.en: Think about it from a kid's perspective, going over there and saying, Hi, I'm Sarah, can I play too, is rude, because it stops the play.
sentences.zh: 从孩子的角度想想，走过去说“嗨，我是莎拉，我也能一起玩吗”，这很粗鲁，因为它打断了游戏。

sentences.en: Everybody else has to turn around, look at your kid, decide if they want her to play.
sentences.zh: 其他人不得不转过身，看着你的孩子，决定是否想让她加入。

sentences.en: And that's just too much of an opening for the mischievous kids who are going to say, No, you can't play.
sentences.zh: 这给那些调皮的孩子提供了太多的机会，他们会说：“不，你不能玩。”

sentences.en: Ho, ho, ho, ho.
sentences.zh: 呵，呵，呵，呵。

sentences.en: So that's not ideal.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不理想。

sentences.en: So instead, they can join by either giving a compliment or just trying to slide into the action and do what everybody else is doing.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们可以通过赞美，或者只是尝试滑入活动中，做大家都在做的事情来加入。

sentences.en: So look around, see what they're doing, do that, do that.
sentences.zh: 所以环顾四周，看看他们在做什么，跟着做，就做那个。

sentences.en: Sounds like good advice for navigating a cocktail party too.
sentences.zh: 听起来这也是应对鸡尾酒会的良策。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, the same principle applies to older kids and teens and adults.
sentences.zh: 同样的原则也适用于大孩子、青少年和成年人。

sentences.en: And here, the watch them blend sequence is about matching the emotional tone of the group.
sentences.zh: 在这里，“观察然后融入”的流程在于匹配群体的基调。

sentences.en: So if everybody is talking about the latest collectible, and our boy comes over and says, well, these are stupid.
sentences.zh: 如果大家都在谈论最新的收藏品，而我们的男孩走过来说：“嗯，这些太蠢了。”

sentences.en: I mean, they're just cardboard with pictures printed on them.
sentences.zh: “我的意思是，它们不过是印着图案的纸板而已。”

sentences.en: That's like a sour note in a melody.
sentences.zh: 这就像旋律中不和谐的音符。

sentences.en: La, la, la, la, la, la.
sentences.zh: 啦，啦，啦，啦，啦，啦。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: So, and he may as well have a sign above his head saying, I don't belong here.
sentences.zh: 所以，他头顶上简直就像写着“我不属于这里”。

sentences.en: So we don't want that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不希望那样。

sentences.en: He can either ask an interested question, starting with how or what, avoid why, because that can sound very judgmental, like why did you do such a thing?
sentences.zh: 他可以问一个感兴趣的问题，以“如何”或“什么”开头，避免用“为什么”，因为那听起来很评判，比如“你为什么要那样做？”

sentences.en: Or he can, yeah, so ask an interested question or just give a compliment and, or make a comment about the thing that matches the tone.
sentences.zh: 或者他可以，是的，问一个感兴趣的问题，或者只是给出一个赞美，或者对那件事发表一个符合基调的评论。

sentences.en: If everybody's enthusiastic, he has to be enthusiastic or he has to find a group where they all hate the collectibles and that's fine too.
sentences.zh: 如果大家都很热情，他也必须表现得热情，或者他必须找到一个大家都讨厌这些收藏品的群体，那也没问题。

sentences.en: Or another example is if everybody's complaining about the social studies test and our girl comes in and says, well, I thought it was easy.
sentences.zh: 或者另一个例子是，如果大家都在抱怨社会研究考试，而我们的女孩走进来却说：“嗯，我觉得很简单。”

sentences.en: Oh, you know, sour note there.
sentences.zh: 噢，你知道，那是个不和谐的音符。

sentences.en: Now she doesn't have to lie and pretend that she's stupid.
sentences.zh: 她不必撒谎假装自己很笨。

sentences.en: Like deceit is not a path towards intimacy, but what she could do is match the tone and say, yeah, I can't believe there were four short answers, or it's so unfair that we
sentences.zh: 欺骗并不是通往亲密的途径，但她可以匹配基调说：“是啊，真不敢相信有四道简答题，或者真不公平，我们竟然在同一天考社会研究和数学。”

sentences.en: had the social studies test on the same day that we had the math test or whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 或者类似的话。

sentences.en: And then she's matching the tone of the group.
sentences.zh: 这样她就匹配了群体的基调。

sentences.en: Now, do you see the same friendship dynamics at work in boys and in girls?
sentences.zh: 那么，你在男孩和女孩身上看到的友谊动态是一样的吗？

sentences.en: I mean, as adults, men tend to have fewer close friends than women do.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，作为成年人，男性往往比女性拥有更少的亲密朋友。

sentences.en: Is that true among children?
sentences.zh: 在孩子中间也是这样吗？

sentences.en: There is some research about differences between boys and girls' friendships and anybody who's ever looked at a playground sees the separation at a certain age.
sentences.zh: 有一些关于男孩和女孩友谊差异的研究，任何观察过操场的人都会看到在一定年龄段的这种分离。

sentences.en: And then they come together as they get older towards, towards the teen years.
sentences.zh: 然后随着年龄增长，到了青少年时期，他们又会走到一起。

sentences.en: Um, so some people have kind of characterized it as a deficit for boys, um, that, you know, girls have more intimate friendships.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有些人把这归结为男孩的某种缺失，嗯，你知道，女孩有更亲密的友谊。

sentences.en: Boys tend to be in larger groups.
sentences.zh: 男孩往往处于更大的群体中。

sentences.en: Um, but the flip side of that is that girls tend to have higher expectations of their friends.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但另一方面，女孩往往对朋友有更高的期望。

sentences.en: So they feel more betrayed when the, the friend doesn't meet those expectations and isn't there for them the way they think they ought to be.
sentences.zh: 所以当朋友没有达到这些期望，没有像她们认为的那样支持她们时，她们会感到更强烈的背叛感。

sentences.en: Boys tend to, and again, these are generalizations, but boys tend to be better at stepping past a conflict and keep the game going kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 男孩往往——同样，这些都是概括——男孩往往更擅长跨越冲突，让游戏继续下去。

sentences.en: And that is a strength.
sentences.zh: 这是一种优势。

sentences.en: Um, so there's been mixed results about whether boys or girls have more conflicts.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以关于男孩还是女孩冲突更多，结果不一。

sentences.en: And I think they're, they're about even as, as, as my read on things.
sentences.zh: 我认为它们差不多，这是我的解读。

sentences.en: Now you host a podcast for kids, right?
sentences.zh: 你主持了一个儿童播客，对吧？

sentences.en: Called Dr. Frentastic, great name, where you answer questions directly from children.
sentences.zh: 叫《Dr. Frentastic》，名字很棒，你在那里直接回答孩子们的问题。

sentences.en: Do you have any favorite questions and answers you could tell us about?
sentences.zh: 你有什么可以告诉我们的最喜欢的问答吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: So this is probably my favorite work activity.
sentences.zh: 这可能是我最喜欢的工作内容。

sentences.en: So the podcast comes out weekly and it's just five minutes.
sentences.zh: 播客每周更新，只有五分钟。

sentences.en: And every episode features an audio recording of a question about friendship from a child.
sentences.zh: 每一集都会播放一段孩子关于友谊的提问录音。

sentences.en: And the kids questions are deep.
sentences.zh: 孩子们的问题很深刻。

sentences.en: I, I just, I just love them.
sentences.zh: 我，我真的很喜欢它们。

sentences.en: Um, so one of them that came up recently, there was a little eight year old girl named Vera and she sent in a question asking, do we have to change ourselves to make friends?
sentences.zh: 嗯，最近出现的一个问题，有个叫薇拉的八岁小女孩发来一个问题，问：“我们必须为了交朋友而改变自己吗？”

sentences.en: Like, how cool is that?
sentences.zh: 这多酷啊？

sentences.en: Oh my gosh, I couldn't wait to answer it.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我迫不及待地想回答它。

sentences.en: So my answer was that my favorite questions in life, not just on the podcast are ones where it
sentences.zh: 所以我的回答是，我生活中最喜欢的问题，不仅仅是在播客上，是那些表面看起来简单，

sentences.en: looks simple on the surface, but the more you think about it, the more questions it raises.
sentences.zh: 但你思考得越多，它引发的问题就越多的那种。

sentences.en: So what do you mean by change?
sentences.zh: 你说的“改变”是什么意思？

sentences.en: What do you mean by self?
sentences.zh: 你说的“自我”是什么意思？

sentences.en: What do you mean by friends?
sentences.zh: 你说的“朋友”是什么意思？

sentences.en: So this is just delicious.
sentences.zh: 这真是太美妙了。

sentences.en: And I went through all of those and I talked about how we are all different in different situations, different relationships.
sentences.zh: 我深入探讨了所有这些，谈到了我们在不同的情况、不同的关系中都是不同的。

sentences.en: And we also change over time.
sentences.zh: 而且我们也会随着时间而改变。

sentences.en: At the same time, we do have a sense of authenticity of moments where we think this is who I am or want to be.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我们确实有一种真实感，在某些时刻我们会想“这就是我，或者我想成为的样子”。

sentences.en: And that's beautiful.
sentences.zh: 那很美。

sentences.en: That's beautiful.
sentences.zh: 那很美。

sentences.en: But we also will sometimes do what a friend wants, even if it's not exactly what we want.
sentences.zh: 但我们有时也会做朋友想做的事，即使那并不完全是我们想要的。

sentences.en: But this is very authentic, because it taps into our deepest values of caring for the friend.
sentences.zh: 但这非常真实，因为它触及了我们关爱朋友的最深层价值观。

sentences.en: So the answer to the question, do we need to change ourselves to make friends is no, we need to show up as our most authentic, caring selves.
sentences.zh: 所以对于“我们需要为了交朋友而改变自己吗”这个问题的回答是：不需要，我们需要展现出最真实、最关怀的自我。

sentences.en: So, but I love the intellectual challenge of can I say something meaningful and practical in five minutes.
sentences.zh: 所以，但我喜欢这种智力挑战，即我能否在五分钟内说出有意义且实用的东西。

sentences.en: And just the children's voices are delicious.
sentences.zh: 而且孩子们的声音真是太美妙了。

sentences.en: And their questions are really, really wonderful.
sentences.zh: 他们的问题真的非常非常棒。

sentences.en: Some of them are very specific to kids.
sentences.zh: 有些问题非常针对孩子。

sentences.en: So I had a little boy who, who called in or sent in a recording, saying that somebody had punched his example owl.
sentences.zh: 我有个小男孩打来电话或发来录音，说有人打了他的猫头鹰玩偶。

sentences.en: Oh, my goodness.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, but some of the issues are just things that we as adults are continuing to grapple with.
sentences.zh: 但有些问题正是我们成年人仍在努力解决的事情。

sentences.en: So I had a little girl who sent in a question about a friend breaking off the friendship because of just one little thing.
sentences.zh: 有个小女孩发来一个问题，关于一个朋友因为一件小事就断绝了友谊。

sentences.en: And I got to talk about perspective taking that, you know, sometimes what feels small to us might feel big to her.
sentences.zh: 我有机会谈到了换位思考，你知道，有时对我们来说感觉很小的事情，对她来说可能感觉很大。

sentences.en: Um, and another, um, kid wrote in about a friend lying to them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有另一个孩子写信来问关于朋友对他们撒谎的事。

sentences.en: And then I was able to talk about, um, well, yes, lying is bad.
sentences.zh: 然后我能够谈到，嗯，是的，撒谎是不好的。

sentences.en: And, but do you make it easy for your child to, for your friend to tell the truth to you?
sentences.zh: 但是，你是否让你朋友容易对你说实话呢？

sentences.en: So I'm always pushing for empathy and, um, reflection and what can you do?
sentences.zh: 所以我总是推动同理心和反思，你还能做什么？

sentences.en: You know, like, so I wrote an article once about the limits of hashtag mental health, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我曾经写过一篇文章，关于“心理健康”标签的局限性，对吧？

sentences.en: And like, I've written 10 books, I've done dozens of, uh, videos and I don't know how many articles, but so I believe deeply in giving psychology away.
sentences.zh: 我写了10本书，做了几十个视频，还有数不清的文章，但我深信心理学知识应该普及。

sentences.en: But what I don't like is a lot of times hashtag mental health is about pointing out how somebody else is bad.
sentences.zh: 但我不喜欢的是，很多时候“心理健康”标签只是为了指出别人有多糟糕。

sentences.en: That's not useful in therapy.
sentences.zh: 这在治疗中没有用。

sentences.en: If you are talking about somebody else's foibles, you're not doing therapy because that person's not in the room, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你在谈论别人的缺点，你就不在做治疗，因为那个人不在房间里，对吧？

sentences.en: We can't control them.
sentences.zh: 我们无法控制他们。

sentences.en: We can only control what you do, how you think about the situation, how you respond to the situation, the choices that you make.
sentences.zh: 我们只能控制你做什么，你如何看待这种情况，你如何应对这种情况，以及你所做的选择。

sentences.en: So last question, we've just hit the four year anniversary of the COVID pandemic.
sentences.zh: 最后一个问题，我们刚刚迎来了新冠疫情四周年。

sentences.en: It's been a lot written early on about how COVID isolation could affect kids' development and, and their friendships.
sentences.zh: 早期有很多关于新冠隔离如何影响儿童发展和友谊的文章。

sentences.en: So four years out, do you think we're still seeing effects from the pandemic?
sentences.zh: 所以四年过去了，你认为我们还在看到疫情的影响吗？

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Um, and I don't have data on that, but my teacher colleagues tell me that children are less able to deal with conflict and, um, less willing to reach out.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我没有相关数据，但我的教师同事告诉我，孩子们处理冲突的能力变弱了，也不太愿意主动接触他人。

sentences.en: Oh my gosh, I have to pressure my clients to say, get together in person because they're used to, too used to staying apart.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我必须向我的客户施压，说：“亲自见面吧”，因为他们习惯了，太习惯于保持距离了。

sentences.en: So I think that that is really, really important.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这真的非常非常重要。

sentences.en: Um, this, uh, finger pointing, I don't know if it's the pandemic or it's the times we live in, but I think that that is really unhelpful.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这种指责，我不知道是疫情的原因还是我们所处的时代，但我认为这真的毫无帮助。

sentences.en: Um, for instance,
sentences.zh: 嗯，例如，

sentences.en: I think the word bullying is thrown around way too easily.
sentences.zh: 我认为“霸凌”这个词被滥用了。

sentences.en: And as a clinical psychologist, I have seen the very serious cases of peer abuse.
sentences.zh: 作为一名临床心理学家，我见过非常严重的同伴欺凌案例。

sentences.en: So like that is very difficult and very important, but what I've seen a lot more often is what I call ordinary meanness.
sentences.zh: 这种情况确实非常棘手且重要，但我见得更多的是我所说的“普通刻薄”。

sentences.en: And this is just clumsy efforts to handle a conflict.
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是处理冲突时笨拙的表现。

sentences.en: For instance, I had a young girl who was very upset because her friend was sitting with someone else on the bus.
sentences.zh: 例如，我曾遇到一个年轻女孩，她非常难过，因为她的朋友在公交车上和别人坐在一起。

sentences.en: And so she decided to write a long letter to the friend listing everything that the friend had ever done because she was convinced that this friend was bullying her
sentences.zh: 于是她决定给那个朋友写一封长信，列出那个朋友做过的所有事情，因为她确信这个朋友在欺负她，

sentences.en: by excluding her.
sentences.zh: 通过排挤她来欺负她。

sentences.en: The friend got the letter and accused my client of bullying her because the letter was really mean.
sentences.zh: 那个朋友收到信后，反过来指责我的客户在欺负她，因为那封信写得真的很刻薄。

sentences.en: So, um, but there was no bullying on either side.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，其实双方都没有欺凌行为。

sentences.en: It was just really a clumsy effort to resolve a conflict.
sentences.zh: 这真的只是解决冲突时笨拙的尝试。

sentences.en: It was hurt feelings.
sentences.zh: 那是受伤的感觉。

sentences.en: Um, and just not knowing how to get past that friendship rough spot.
sentences.zh: 嗯，只是不知道如何度过那段友谊的摩擦期。

sentences.en: So I don't believe in trying to separate the good kids from the bad kids because we all make mistakes, but I believe in helping kids learn to speak up in kind ways to, um, forgive
sentences.zh: 所以我并不主张试图把好孩子和坏孩子区分开来，因为我们都会犯错，但我主张帮助孩子们学会用友善的方式表达，去原谅

sentences.en: their friends.
sentences.zh: 他们的朋友。

sentences.en: Um, in one of my books, Growing Friendships, I talk about forgiveness guidelines.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在我的书《培养友谊》（Growing Friendships）中，我谈到了原谅的准则。

sentences.en: I had a client once who, um, it was the mom and the kid and I were talking about who he, who could he get together with?
sentences.zh: 我曾经有一位客户，嗯，当时是妈妈和孩子在跟我谈论他可以和谁一起玩？

sentences.en: And the mom said, well, how about the boy down the street?
sentences.zh: 妈妈说，那街那头的那个男孩怎么样？

sentences.en: And the kid responded, no, cause two years ago in travel soccer, he never passed the ball.
sentences.zh: 孩子回答说，不行，因为两年前在旅行足球队里，他从来不传球。

sentences.en: Do you think that other kid remembers that?
sentences.zh: 你觉得那个孩子还记得这件事吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 绝对不记得。

sentences.en: So the forgiveness guidelines are things like, if it wasn't that big of a deal, let it go.
sentences.zh: 所以原谅的准则就像是：如果事情没那么严重，就随它去吧。

sentences.en: If it happened once and it's never likely to happen again, let it go.
sentences.zh: 如果只发生过一次，而且以后不太可能再发生，就随它去吧。

sentences.en: If the person is genuinely sorry for it, let it go.
sentences.zh: 如果对方真心感到抱歉，就随它去吧。

sentences.en: If it happened more than a month ago, definitely let it go.
sentences.zh: 如果事情发生在一个月前，那就绝对随它去吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: We don't want to be holding onto grievances like beads on a string.
sentences.zh: 我们不想像串珠子一样一直记着怨恨。

sentences.en: It's, this is part of being a good friend is opening our hearts to forgiveness.
sentences.zh: 这是成为好朋友的一部分，就是敞开心扉去原谅。

sentences.en: There's another thing that I, I see a lot, which is anxiety about friendship.
sentences.zh: 还有一件事我经常看到，那就是对友谊的焦虑。

sentences.en: And what happens is the kids will seek reassurance, right?
sentences.zh: 发生的情况是，孩子们会寻求安慰，对吧？

sentences.en: We know that that's one of the characteristics of anxiety is constantly seeking reassurance to try to make the anxiety go away.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这是焦虑的特征之一，就是不断寻求安慰，试图让焦虑消失。

sentences.en: But it actually raises the anxiety because as soon as you get the reassurance, the worry pops up again, because what if, what if,
sentences.zh: 但实际上这反而增加了焦虑，因为一旦你得到了安慰，担忧又会冒出来，因为“万一……万一……”

sentences.en: what if, so what it might look like with kids is one girl says to another girl, are you mad at me?
sentences.zh: “万一……”，所以这在孩子身上可能表现为，一个女孩对另一个女孩说：“你生我气了吗？”

sentences.en: And she says, no, are you sure you're not mad at me?
sentences.zh: 她说：“没有，你确定没生我气吗？”

sentences.en: No, really?
sentences.zh: “没有，真的吗？”

sentences.en: Are you, you might, are you absolutely positive you're not mad at me?
sentences.zh: “你，你可能，你绝对肯定没生我气吗？”

sentences.en: And now I am.
sentences.zh: 现在我真的生气了。

sentences.en: So it's actually a gift that we give our friends friends by giving them our truSt. That even if we're not together, and even if we haven't spoken
sentences.zh: 所以，给予朋友信任其实是我们送给朋友的一份礼物。即使我们不在一起，即使我们有一小会儿

sentences.en: in a little, little while, there's still a connection.
sentences.zh: 没说话，依然存在着联系。

sentences.en: There's still a liking.
sentences.zh: 依然存在着好感。

sentences.en: And that can be a hard thing to do.
sentences.zh: 这可能是一件很难做到的事情。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Kennedy Moore, I want to thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 好的，肯尼迪·摩尔博士，感谢您今天参加我们的节目。

sentences.en: This has been very edifying, I think, to everyone, not just kids and parents, but to all, all listeners.
sentences.zh: 我想这对每个人来说都非常有启发，不仅是对孩子和家长，对所有听众也是如此。

sentences.en: We should all be paying attention to your advice.
sentences.zh: 我们都应该关注您的建议。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, um, I do have a book that was published by Imagination Press.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，我确实有一本书是由Imagination Press出版的。

sentences.en: Is that Moody, Moody Cars?
sentences.zh: 是那本《情绪化的车》（Moody, Moody Cars）吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 就是那本。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this is for the little ones, four to eight.
sentences.zh: 所以这是给四到八岁的小朋友看的。

sentences.en: And this one, I partnered with, um, Michael Furman, who takes these gorgeous photos of vintage cars.
sentences.zh: 这一本，我与迈克尔·弗曼合作，他拍摄了这些精美的老爷车照片。

sentences.en: And to me, they look like they have faces and expressive faces.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，它们看起来像是有表情，而且是富有表现力的脸。

sentences.en: So, um, the text goes, um, goes freewheeling, full of feeling, traveling near and far.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，文字是这样写的，嗯，自由驰骋，充满情感，穿行于近处和远方。

sentences.en: If you see me, I'm a moody, moody car.
sentences.zh: 如果你看到我，我是一辆情绪化的车。

sentences.en: So it's very fun.
sentences.zh: 所以这非常有趣。

sentences.en: And research tells us that when children at five years old, if they are better at recognizing emotions,
sentences.zh: 研究告诉我们，当孩子五岁时，如果他们更擅长识别情绪，

sentences.en: then the, then four years later, they're better at better socially and emotionally and they're functioning.
sentences.zh: 那么四年后，他们在社交和情感方面会表现得更好，功能也更健全。

sentences.en: So this is, this is important.
sentences.zh: 所以这一点很重要。

sentences.en: It's the foundation is giving kids a glimpse into that emotional world.
sentences.zh: 这是基础，让孩子们得以窥见那个情感世界。

sentences.en: And my most recent book is Growing Feelings, which talks about children's feelings about friends because where do the big feelings come up, right?
sentences.zh: 我最近的一本书是《培养情感》（Growing Feelings），它谈论了孩子们对朋友的情感，因为强烈的情感通常在哪里出现呢，对吧？

sentences.en: In friendships, it's not usually just in the abstract.
sentences.zh: 在友谊中，通常不仅仅是在抽象层面。

sentences.en: It's, it's because of our relationships.
sentences.zh: 是因为我们的关系。

sentences.en: So this one talks about how to understand and cope with and communicate about our feelings in ways that build strong and caring relationships.
sentences.zh: 所以这本书谈论了如何理解、应对和交流我们的感受，以建立稳固且充满关怀的关系。

sentences.en: Well, again, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 好的，再次非常感谢您。

sentences.en: This has been very, very interesting and a lot of fun to talk to you.
sentences.zh: 这次谈话非常、非常有意思，也很愉快。

sentences.en: My pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。
